title: Sampling & aliasing
short: Change the tone and the sample clock. Watch a different wave pass through the same dots.
question: Which frequency will the samples preserve?
instructions: Start at 8 kHz and choose 5,500 Hz. Look for a lower-frequency curve that shares every sample. Compare with 2,500 Hz, then double the sample rate.
expect: At 8 kHz, 5,500 Hz and 2,500 Hz produce the same cosine samples. At 16 kHz, the 5,500 Hz tone fits below Nyquist.

title: Window into frequency
short: Compute a spectrogram from a known signal and trade timing detail for frequency detail.
question: Can you separate two tones and locate their onset?
instructions: Choose the tone pair. Compare 64 and 512 samples per window before trying the sweep. Read the brightest regions against the frequency and time axes.
expect: At 8 kHz the bin spacing narrows from 125 to 15.625 Hz. Longer windows show the two tones more distinctly and spread the onset across more time.

title: Silence or end of turn?
short: Change a speech threshold and silence hold. See which pauses end a turn too early.
question: Is the listener pausing, backchanneling or finished?
instructions: Step through a fixed energy trace containing a mid-turn pause and quiet final speech. Increase the silence hold, then raise the threshold. Compare detected endpoints with the annotated end.
expect: A short hold fires in the middle of the utterance. A high threshold misses a quiet speech segment. A longer hold improves that case but delays the true endpoint.

title: A transcript in motion
short: Follow revisions as a scripted recognizer receives more context, then decide when to commit.
question: When is a partial transcript safe to act on?
instructions: Step through ‘read back paragraph fourteen’. Compare acting on the first number with waiting for the final event. Rewind and inspect which words were revised.
expect: The provisional ‘forty’ becomes ‘fourteen’. Waiting preserves the correct target; the extra waiting costs time. Stability within this fixture is not a universal ASR guarantee.

title: Time to first audio
short: Set component delays and compare the serial and overlapping critical paths.
question: Which stage would actually move the first audible sample?
instructions: Increase endpoint wait, then increase model lead time. Compare serial dispatch with speculative preparation. Watch which bar determines first audible output.
expect: Serial stages sum. In overlap mode, endpoint wait and speculative model preparation start together. Only the slower branch gates synthesis; the model assumes the speculation survives.

title: The unheard buffer
short: Generate, play, interrupt and resume an original passage. Inspect the heard cursor after every event.
question: Which word should Murmur play after a question?
instructions: Queue three words and present one. Interrupt, deliver an old callback, ask about what you heard, then resume. Inspect the document span and both cursors after every step.
expect: Cancellation empties queued narration, preserves the heard prefix and rejects the stale generation. Resume starts with the first unheard word. The answer has a separate playback track.

title: Voice regression bench
short: Run labeled transcript and playback fixtures through a scorer. Inspect each failure by category.
question: Would the same release pass word accuracy and listener safety gates?
instructions: Run the baseline fixtures. Enable a stale-buffer bug and compare exact mismatches and WER. Change normalization, inspect a named-entity failure, and compare cohort counts.
expect: The stale audio regression changes session behavior without changing WER. Number formatting moves a transcript score while the semantic target may stay the same.
